OWD5 cloud only. Devices are created per: 仅限 OWD5 云。设备是根据 GroupId 创建的。 Writeback使用Group/UpdateGroup。能源使用 EnergyUsage/GetEnergyUsage 和 ThermostatID (Thermostats[].Id)。
localAllowCommandsHelp: If the thermostat is connected locally, apply commands are sent directly to it (WD5: schedule, manual, comfort, boost, eco, frost protection). On failure or if unsupported, the cloud is used.
localCheckDnsHelp: Checks with the values in the form whether the hostname points to this host and the port answers (instance must be running).
localCloudPollSecHelp: While all thermostats are connected locally, the cloud is only polled at this interval (energy, vacation dates). 0 = normal poll interval.
localHint:
Setup:
1. Give the ioBroker host a fixed IP.
2. In your DNS, redirect the hostname of the device gateway (below, e.g. owd5-sl003-thermostat.ojelectronics.com) to the ioBroker host – preferably as CNAME to the name of the ioBroker host, otherwise as a record to its IP.
3. Choose a mode, enable "Send commands locally", save.
4. Power-cycle the thermostat.
5. Check: "Check DNS" button; the Device Manager toolbar shows the number of locally connected thermostats.
Relay: the connection is passed on to the vendor cloud (app keeps working) and everything is read locally. Local only: the thermostat is answered by ioBroker and never contacts the cloud (WG4: needs one successful relay session first). Back to the cloud: mode "Off", delete the DNS record, power-cycle the thermostat.
localUpstreamHostHelp: The hostname the thermostat connects to (see the DNS log of your router / Pi-hole / AdGuard).
localUpstreamPinHelp: Empty = the first certificate seen is trusted and stored.
localWarning: IN TESTING: Local control is still being tested. It is meant for users who know DNS and hostnames: it only works with a DNS record in your own network (Pi-hole, AdGuard, router). Use at your own risk and please report your observations.
